questions.decision: A group vote means a poll and rules for ties and non-voters. A rotating chooser needs only a schedule. A single decider needs no tooling, just a clear rule for who decides.

reasons: A book vote for twelve adults involves little sensitive data and has low stakes if it goes wrong.
The main risks are disputes over fairness and members who don't vote. Both are handled by the group, not by software.

hidden_requirements.text: Decide who collects suggestions, who runs the vote and who announces the winner each month.
hidden_requirements.reason: Without a named person, the process stalls whenever the organizer is away.

hidden_requirements.text: Decide how ties, non-voters and repeat or previously read books are handled (proposed rules, to be agreed by the group).
hidden_requirements.reason: These cases come up regularly in a monthly vote and cause friction if they aren't settled in advance.

hidden_requirements.text: Check that members are comfortable with their names and votes being visible to the group or to a poll service.
hidden_requirements.reason: Votes and names leave the owner's control if a third-party poll tool is used. Anonymous voting may suit some members better.

hidden_requirements.text: Plan for membership changes, including new members joining, people leaving and the organizer stepping back.
hidden_requirements.reason: If the process lives on one person's account, it breaks when that person's role changes.

recommendation.summary: Use a simple monthly routine in the chat or email thread the club already uses. Members suggest books, then run a poll with the chat app's built-in poll feature or a free poll tool. Don't build custom software.
rationale: For twelve people once a month, a poll in an existing channel meets the need with no build, no new accounts and no ongoing cost.
A custom app would add hosting, maintenance and account management that this group doesn't need.
alternatives: A shared spreadsheet with a suggestions column and one vote per member.
A rotating chooser, where each member picks in turn and no vote is needed.
A free poll tool, if the chat app has no polling feature.
owner_responsibilities: Open suggestions on a fixed day each month.
Start the poll and announce the result.
Settle tie-break and repeat-book rules with the group.
Hand the routine to someone else if you step back.

acceptance_criteria: Each month, every member can suggest a book and vote in under five minutes without creating a new account (proposed target).
A single named person runs the monthly routine, and a backup is named.
Proposed rule: ties are broken in a way the group agreed in advance, such as a re-vote or a coin flip.
If the poll tool or chat is unavailable, the fallback is to collect votes by reply message, and this has been tried once.
Next check: after the first month, ask members whether the process was easy and fair, and adjust.
If the poll tool changes or shuts down, the routine can move to another tool without losing the list of past books.

limitations: This advice assumes the club already has a shared way to communicate. That has not been confirmed.
